# demo_accel registers

Control and status of a stream accelerator with a descriptor ring and one interrupt.

AXI4-Lite, 32-bit registers, a 0x1000-byte window (address bits [11:2] decoded). Unmapped addresses answer SLVERR and read 0. Version 0.1.0; model sha256 `d6c107624c955f25`.

## Register map

| Offset | Register | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x000 | ID | 0x64a00100 | Block identity; software checks it before touching anything else. |
| 0x004 | CTRL | 0x01000020 | Configuration; written while the block is idle. |
| 0x008 | CMD | 0x00000000 | Commands; reading returns 0. |
| 0x00c | STATUS | 0x00000000 | Live state, read from the hardware. |
| 0x010 | IRQ_STATUS | 0x00000000 | Interrupt causes; write 1 to clear. |
| 0x014 | IRQ_ENABLE | 0x00000000 | Interrupt enables, bit for bit with IRQ_STATUS. |
| 0x020 | RING_BASE | 0x00000000 | Physical address of the descriptor ring (64-byte aligned). |
| 0x024 | RING_TAIL | 0x00000000 | Producer index, written by software after it fills descriptors. |
| 0x028 | RING_HEAD | 0x00000000 | Consumer index, advanced by the hardware. |
| 0x02c | DOORBELL | 0x00000000 | Per-queue doorbells; software rings, the hardware clears when it has seen the new tail. |
| 0x0fc | SCRATCH | 0x00000000 | Free read/write word for bus tests. |

Reset is what a read returns after reset with every hardware input low.

## Access types

| Access | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RW | read/write: software writes the value; hardware sees it on an output |
| RO | read-only: the value comes from a hardware input (or is a constant); writes are ignored |
| W1C | write 1 to clear: hardware sets bits with a pulse input; software clears a bit by writing 1 to it; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set (no event is lost) |
| W1S | write 1 to set: software sets bits by writing 1 (a doorbell); hardware clears them with a pulse input; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set |
| W1P | write 1 to pulse: each bit written as 1 gives a one-clock pulse on an output; reads return 0 |

## ID (0x000)

Block identity; software checks it before touching anything else.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31:16 | MAGIC | RO const | 0x64a0 | fixed pattern 0x64A0 |
| 15:0 | VERSION | RO const | 0x100 | register-map version 1.0 |

## CTRL (0x004)

Configuration; written while the block is idle.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27:16 | SCALE | RW | 0x100 | output gain, unsigned 4.8 fixed point |
| 8 | OVERFLOW | W1C | 0x0 | an input beat arrived while the block was disabled |
| 6:4 | MODE | RW | 0x2 | kernel select |
| 0 | ENABLE | RW | 0x0 | 1 lets the block accept stream data |

## CMD (0x008)

Commands; reading returns 0.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | FLUSH | W1P | 0 | drop buffered data |
| 0 | START | W1P | 0 | start one job |

| 0 | BUSY | RO | hw | a job is running |

## Interrupt

`irq_o` is a level output, registered: high while any bit of IRQ_STATUS is set and the same bit of IRQ_ENABLE is set. Clear the cause by writing 1 to the IRQ_STATUS bit (W1C); the line drops one clock after the clear.
